t: Muhammad ﷺ is born in Mecca in the Year of the Elephant, after his father Abdullah has died. Ibn Ishaq: 12 Rabi' al-Awwal; Sealed Nectar: 9 Rabi' al-Awwal, April 571.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), p. 69; Sealed Nectar, 'His Birth', p. 56; Britannica, 'Muhammad' (c. 570)

t: As an infant he is entrusted to the wet nurse Halima bint Abi Dhu'ayb of Banu Sa'd and raised among the desert Bedouin.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'His birth and fostermother', pp. 69-73; Sealed Nectar, 'Babyhood', p. 57

t: At about six his mother Amina dies at al-Abwa' returning from Yathrib. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib takes him in; at eight he passes to his uncle Abu Talib.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), pp. 73, 79; Sealed Nectar, 'Back to his passionate Mother' and 'To His compassionate Grandfather', p. 59

t: At about 25, Muhammad ﷺ marries Khadija bint Khuwaylid, a respected merchant of Mecca. She is his only wife until her death.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), p. 82 and Ibn Hisham's note 126; Sealed Nectar, 'His Marriage to Khadijah', p. 62

t: When he is 35, Quraysh rebuild the Ka'ba. A dispute over replacing the Black Stone is settled by his arbitration, the clans lifting it together on a cloak.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'Rebuilding of the Ka'ba', p. 84; Sealed Nectar, 'Rebuilding Al-Ka'bah and the Arbitration Issue', p. 63

t: At about 40, the first revelation comes to Muhammad ﷺ in the cave of Hira' in Ramadan. Sealed Nectar dates it to Monday 21 Ramadan, 10 August 610.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), pp. 104-105; Sealed Nectar, 'In the Shade of the Message and Prophethood', p. 67

t: After about three years of private calling, he is commanded to preach openly, beginning with his near kin and the address from Mount al-Safa.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), p. 117; Sealed Nectar, 'Three years of Secret Call' and 'The Second Phase: Open Preaching', pp. 77-82

t: Facing persecution, a group of twelve men and four women, including Uthman and Ruqayya, migrates to Abyssinia under the Negus, in Rajab.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'The first emigrants to Abyssinia', p. 146; Sealed Nectar, 'The First Migration to Abyssinia', p. 99

t: Quraysh impose a boycott on Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, who are confined in the Shi'b of Abu Talib for about three years until the pact is annulled.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), pp. 159, 172; Sealed Nectar, 'General Social Boycott', p. 117

t: The Year of Grief: Abu Talib and Khadija both die. In Shawwal Muhammad ﷺ travels to al-Ta'if with Zayd ibn Haritha to invite Thaqif to Islam and is harshly rejected.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), pp. 191-192; Sealed Nectar, 'The Year of Grief', p. 123, and 'Calling unto Islam beyond Makkah', p. 136

t: The Isra' and Mi'raj: the Night Journey to Jerusalem and Ascension through the heavens. Its date is disputed; Sealed Nectar notes most place it 12-16 months before the Hijra.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'The night journey and the ascent to heaven', p. 181; Sealed Nectar, 'Al-Isra' and Al-Mi'raj', p. 147

t: At al-Aqaba near Mina, Muslims of Yathrib give the First Pledge (621) and, the next pilgrimage season, the Second Pledge (622), promising to protect him.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'The first pledge at al-Aqaba' and 'The second pledge at al-Aqaba', p. 201; Sealed Nectar, 'The First Aqabah Pledge', p. 154, and 'The Second Aqabah Pledge', p. 157

t: The Hijra: Muhammad ﷺ and Abu Bakr migrate to Yathrib (Medina). Arrival at Quba' is 12 Rabi' al-Awwal per Ibn Ishaq, 8 Rabi' al-Awwal (23 September 622) per Sealed Nectar.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'Date of the hijra', p. 281; Sealed Nectar, 'Migration of the Prophet', p. 168

t: Battle of Badr, 17 Ramadan: a small Muslim force defeats a larger Meccan army in the first decisive battle in the history of Islam.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'Battle of Badr', from p. 289; Sealed Nectar, 'The Battle of Badr', p. 210

t: Battle of Uhud in Shawwal: the Muslims suffer heavy losses against Quraysh. The day is given as 7 Shawwal (Sealed Nectar) or mid-Shawwal (Ibn Ishaq).
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'Battle of Uhud', from p. 370; Sealed Nectar, 'The Battle of Uhud', p. 245

t: Battle of the Trench (al-Ahzab), Shawwal: a confederate army besieges Medina for about a month, but a defensive trench holds and the siege collapses.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'Battle of the Ditch' (section heading); Sealed Nectar, 'Al-Ahzab (the Confederates) Invasion', p. 311

t: Treaty of al-Hudaybiyya in Dhu al-Qa'da establishes a truce with Quraysh. Afterwards letters inviting to Islam go to rulers including Caesar, Chosroes and the Muqawqis.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'The affair of al-Hudaybiya', p. 499, and 'Missions to foreign rulers', p. 652; Sealed Nectar, 'Al-Hudaibiyah Treaty', p. 339, and pp. 350-360

t: Conquest of Mecca in Ramadan with about 10,000 men, entering with little fighting and granting safety to the inhabitants. The Battle of Hunayn follows soon after.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'The occupation of Mecca', p. 540, and 'Battle of Hunayn', p. 566; Sealed Nectar, 'The Conquest of Makkah', p. 388

t: Expedition to Tabuk in Rajab against Byzantine forces, without battle. The following months, called the Year of Delegations, see tribes across Arabia send deputations.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'Raid on Tabuk', p. 602, and 'The Year of the Deputations', p. 627; Sealed Nectar, 'The Invasion of Tabuk', p. 422, and 'The Delegations', p. 443

t: Farewell Pilgrimage in Dhu al-Hijja 10 AH. Muhammad ﷺ passes away in Medina on Monday 12 Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH (June 632), aged 63 lunar years.
src: Ibn Hisham (Guillaume), 'The farewell pilgrimage', p. 649, and 'His death', p. 682; Sealed Nectar, 'The Farewell Pilgrimage', p. 461, and 'The Prophet breathes his Last', p. 478; Britannica (8 June 632)
